State pension / Social Security
C1
Client 1
Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) determines whether this income stream grows with inflation.

• Full COLA — the benefit increases by the full inflation rate each year, so its real (purchasing) value stays constant. Typical of US Social Security and most public pensions.
• Partial — the benefit rises at half the inflation rate; real value slowly declines (common for capped or partially-indexed plans).
• None — the benefit is fixed in nominal terms. With 3% inflation, its real value roughly halves over ~23 years (typical of many private annuities).

Why it matters: over a 25–30 year retirement, the COLA choice can change the lifetime value of a pension by tens of percent. Choosing None on an income that should be indexed will understate your real spending power later in life.
Auto-populates from Client 1's country (Household tab).

Goals & funding
Goal Funding probability-based + present-value · click to expandiGoal-relative optimization — goals are funded in priority order each simulated year (essential, then important, then aspirational/legacy), not split evenly. A shortfall shows up against the lower-priority goal competing for the same dollars, not against every goal active that year. This is one of the value-creating activities identified in goals-based wealth management (GBWM) research (independent studies from Vanguard, Morningstar, Envestnet and Russell Investments on advisor-created value).
Each goal is scored two ways: the simulated probability of being fully funded (from the simulated outcomes) and the present-value funding ratio (priority-weighted, discounted at a risk-adjusted rate). Run the simulation to populate both.
Run the simulation to populate funding status.
Fully funded probability ≥ 80% / ratio ≥ 90% Partly funded 50–79% / 60–89% At risk 25–49% Underfunded < 25% / < 60% Simulated success reads the percentile of simulated net worth in the goal's calendar year against the amount needed. Note: "net worth" here includes all simulated wealth (investments, cash, property, retirement accounts minus debt) — for goals needing liquid funds quickly, actual availability may be lower if a significant portion of wealth is in illiquid assets. The PV funding ratio discounts each goal's cost at a rate matched to its priority tier (Essential 95% / Important 75% / Aspirational 55% confidence), grossed for tax, and compares it to current assets plus reachable future savings, using the capital-market-assumption covariance engine.
🎯 Goals-Based Analysis institutional funding-ratio method · click to expand
Institutional goals-based methodology using per-asset-class capital market assumptions with a full correlation matrix for accurate portfolio risk. This feeds the Goal Funding panel above (present-value cost, priority-weighted discount rate, funding ratio) — this section shows the underlying assumptions and your Wealth Allocation Framework.
Capital Market Assumptions
Per-asset-class long-term return/risk assumptions used to derive your portfolio's risk-adjusted return. Geometric mean = arithmetic − ½σ². Core long-term inflation assumption: 2.28%.
Educational projection only — not financial advice. Funding ratios and achievable lifestyle figures are hypothetical, derived from capital market assumptions and your inputs. Actual results will differ. Consult a licensed advisor.
Wealth Allocation Framework Personal / Market / Aspirational · click to expand
The three-bucket wealth allocation framework organizes assets by risk-return role: Personal (preserve lifestyle — residence, cash), Market (balance risk & return — diversified equities/bonds), and Aspirational (idiosyncratic upside — concentrated stock, business, crypto, investment property).
Add assets to see your wealth allocation.
Retirement income & withdrawals
Retirement Drawdown — will your money last? click to expand
A decumulation simulation: from your retirement age, each year withdraws your retirement spending (net of pensions & Social Security), the portfolio earns a random return, and we count how often it lasts to your planning age — capturing sequence-of-returns risk (a poor market early in retirement does lasting damage). The whole investable pool is exposed to market risk here.
Set your retirement age, spending, and pensions above, then run the drawdown analysis.
Your Personal Retirement Number actuarial lump sum · click to expand
The lump-sum you would theoretically need today to purchase an inflation-adjusted annuity from a highly-rated issuer — funding your retirement income from your target retirement age through age 98 (a longevity horizon set from your residence country's life expectancy). Calculated using a 6.8% discount rate and your configured inflation assumption, based on standard actuarial present-value formulas.
Retirement NumberiRetirement Number — the lump sum you'd need on the day you retire. Your annual retirement spending is grown by inflation to the retirement date, then priced as an inflation-adjusted annuity paying every year from your retirement age to the planning age shown above (your country's life expectancy plus a longevity buffer), using a 6.8% discount rate.
—
lump sum needed at retirement
Present Value TodayiPresent Value Today — the Retirement Number discounted back from your retirement date to today at the same 6.8% rate: the amount that, invested today at that return, would grow into the full lump sum by the day you retire. This is the figure your net worth is compared against.
—
discounted to today's dollars
Current Net WorthiCurrent Net Worth — everything you own today minus everything you owe: all accounts (plus portfolio holdings, de-duplicated against any linked account), property, other assets and insurance cash value, less outstanding loan balances.
—
vs. target above
Funding Gap / SurplusiFunding Gap / Surplus — Current Net Worth minus Present Value Today. Positive (green): you're ahead of the actuarial target — today's wealth, compounding at the assumed rate, would cover retirement. Negative (red): the additional amount you'd need today; future savings and investment growth above the assumption can still close it.
—
vs. present-value target
Formula: PV = AnnualSpend × [1 − (1 + realRate)−n] / realRate, where realRate = (discountRate − inflation) / (1 + inflation) and n = years from retirement age to age 98. The result is then discounted back to today at the nominal discount rate. Annuity pricing assumes a 6.8% discount rate with your configured inflation rate (default 3.8%). Run the simulation or update expenses to refresh.
Required Minimum Withdrawals RMD / RRIF / min pension · click to expand
Many countries force a minimum annual withdrawal from tax-deferred retirement accounts once you reach a set age — the US RMD, Canada's RRIF minimum, Australia's minimum pension drawdown. This projects that mandatory schedule from your retirement pool and estimates the tax it triggers, using your household country's rule. Illustrative — not tax advice.
Set your country (Household tab) and retirement accounts, then project the schedule.
Roth-Style Conversion Window low-income-year conversions · click to expand
Converting tax-deferred savings to a tax-free account in low-income years — the gap between retiring and when mandatory withdrawals or pensions begin — locks in today's lower tax rate and shrinks future required withdrawals. This sizes that window from your retirement pool, using your country's equivalent mechanism (or flags where none exists). Illustrative — not tax advice.
Set your country, retirement age, and retirement accounts, then analyze.

Portfolio efficiency & risk
Tax Efficiency Overlay asset-location analysis · click to expand
Asset location analysis: growth-heavy assets sitting in taxable accounts create a persistent drag on compound returns. This engine classifies your accounts by tax treatment and estimates the drag of capital gains taxes over a 30-year horizon.

Asset Location Score —/100
Annual tax drag: — 30-yr cumulative drag: — Shortfall cost-basis tax: —
Score methodology: 100 = all growth assets in Roth/ISA/TFSA (fully tax-free). Tax-deferred accounts score 70% (gains grow untaxed but withdrawals are taxed as income). Taxable accounts score 0%. Annual drag = taxable balance × portfolio return × 25% assumed marginal rate. Shortfall cost-basis logic: when a cash-flow shortfall occurs, the engine assumes the gap is funded from a taxable account at 100% cost basis, adding a tax cost of shortfall × effective rate.
🇨🇭 Swiss Pension — Lump-Sum Withdrawal Tax by Canton pillar 2 & 3a · click to expand
Taking your 2nd pillar (BVG/LPP) or pillar 3a as a lump sum is taxed once, separately from your other income, at a reduced rate that varies widely by canton. This estimates that one-time capital-withdrawal tax and shows how staggering across years — and where you reside — changes it.

🇨🇭 Swiss Pension — Annuity vs Lump Sum 2nd pillar · break-even · click to expand
At retirement your 2nd pillar (BVG/LPP) can be drawn as a lifelong annuity or a one-time lump sum. The annuity is taxed as income for life and insures against outliving your money; the lump sum is taxed once (panel above), then it's yours to invest and leave to heirs. This compares the two and finds the break-even age. It is a comparison, not a recommendation — the right choice also depends on your health, family and risk appetite.

Mean-Variance Optimization — Efficient Frontier click to expand
The trade-off between risk and reward, in one picture. Every way of investing sits somewhere between “safe but slow” and “bumpy but potentially faster.” This chart plots that trade-off so you can see exactly where your plan lands.
How to read it
→ Left-to-right = risk. How much your investments swing up and down from year to year. Further right means bigger swings.
↑ Bottom-to-top = reward. The average yearly return you’d expect over the long run. Higher up means more growth.
Each dot is one investing style, ranging from very cautious (bottom-left) to very aggressive (top-right).
The curved line is the “best deals.” It links the styles that give the most reward for each level of risk — that line is the efficient frontier.
The big dot is you — where your household’s current risk profile sits today.
The takeaway: you generally can’t earn more without accepting more ups and downs — that’s why the line slopes upward. A dot sitting on the line is an efficient choice. A dot below the line means you’re taking on risk without getting the extra reward you could — so aim for the line. To reach for more growth you move right (a bumpier ride), so pick the spot that matches how much bumpiness you can comfortably live with.
For the technically minded: this is Harry Markowitz’s Mean-Variance Optimization (Modern Portfolio Theory). Each dot’s position is its expected arithmetic mean return (μ, vertical axis) and annualised standard deviation of returns (σ, horizontal axis), sourced from long-run institutional capital market assumptions. The dashed curve is the efficient frontier fitted through those points; your household profile is the larger dot.

Methodology & Disclaimer click to expand
Inputs the simulation reads
Income (sum of all four income fields), annual raise %, base expenses (Living + Insurance + Other), inflation rate (taken from the Region preset — 50-yr historical CPI averages — or your manual override), property value, other assets, the sum of every entry on the Assets tab, and each loan's balance / rate / remaining years. Projection length and number of simulations come from the Settings panel.
Return parameters by risk profile
Profile Mean return Volatility
Very conservative3.5%4%
Conservative4.5%7%
Moderately conservative5.5%9%
Moderate7.0%12%
Moderately aggressive8.5%15%
Aggressive10.0%18%
Very aggressive12.0%22%
When two clients are in the household, the mean and volatility are averaged.
Stochastic engine — what happens each year
Investment return is sampled log-normally via Box–Muller as (μ − 0.5σ²) + σ × N(0,1). Property appreciates by a random 3% ± 2% each year. Income grows by your raise %, expenses grow by inflation. Each loan amortizes with its real interest math. When the year ends with a positive surplus, 30% goes to investments and 70% to cash. Initial investment allocation is max(actual investment-account balances, 30% of total account assets). Net worth at each step is cash + investments + property + other − remaining loan balances.
How goals are scored
For each goal, the engine counts the share of simulation paths whose liquid wealth covers every scheduled outflow through the goal's end year without a shortfall.
Disclaimer. This tool is for educational and planning purposes only. It is not investment, tax, or legal advice. Historical averages and randomly sampled returns do not predict actual market behaviour; real outcomes can differ materially due to sequence-of-returns risk, tax drag, behavioural decisions, fees, and unmodeled life events. Consult a licensed financial professional before acting on any projection shown here.

Top holdingiTop holding — your single largest position as a share of the portfolio. A high figure signals single-name (idiosyncratic) risk: one holding driving outsized impact.
—
Concentration (HHI)iConcentration (HHI) — the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index: the sum of each holding's squared weight (0-10,000). Higher = more concentrated. Below ~1,500 is diversified; above ~2,500 is concentrated.
—
DiversificationiDiversification grade — a letter grade (A-F) derived from the HHI concentration. A means well spread across positions; D/F means a few holdings dominate.
—
Wtd yieldiWeighted yield — the value-weighted average income yield (dividends + interest) across holdings. Approximates the annual cash income the portfolio throws off as a % of value.
—
Wtd expense ratioiWeighted expense ratio — the value-weighted average annual fund fee across holdings. This cost is deducted from gross returns every year, so lower is better.
—
Risk scoreiRisk score — the portfolio's covariance-based volatility mapped to a 0-10 scale. It accounts for how asset classes correlate, so a diversified mix scores lower than the average of its parts. The bar below shades from green (low risk, near 0) to red (high risk, near 10) along this same 0-10 scale.
—
When the portfolio has holdings, its total is added to the simulation's investment seed and the asset-class mix overrides the risk-profile return assumptions. Avoid double-counting positions you've already entered as Investment account values on the Assets tab.

%/yr
Deducted from gross portfolio return in all simulations and projections.
Gross expected returnithe portfolio's value-weighted expected annual return, derived from each holding's asset-class capital-market assumption (cash excluded).
—
Advisory fee dragiThe annual cost of your advisory fee (AUM % or flat $), converted to an effective % drag on returns — subtracted from gross return every year in all simulations.
—
Net expected return (after fee)iGross expected return minus the advisory fee drag, floored at zero — this is the return actually used to project your portfolio in the market simulation.

✦ AI Data Agent
Upload any client documents — brokerage & bank statements, tax forms, questionnaires, photos & screenshots, scanned PDFs, Word/PowerPoint/OpenDocument files, CSV/XLSX/ODS, or notes. The agent reads them (vision for images & scans), extracts every data point it can across the whole profile, and shows you a review screen before anything is written to the app.
⭳ Import statement (CSV / OFX / QFX)
Import a bank or brokerage statement directly — no AI key needed. Reads CSV exports, OFX, and QFX (Quicken) files, lets you map the columns, and shows the same review screen before anything is added. For photos, PDFs, or unusual files, use the AI Data Agent instead.
🔌 Data feeds — custodians & CRM
Pull positions, balances and client records straight from a custodian or CRM endpoint. Every connector normalizes into the same wa.feed/v1 data model and lands in the standard review screen, so nothing is written until you approve it. Credentials stay in this browser (localStorage) and are sent only to the endpoint you configure.

Order Routing click to expand
Where order tickets are sent. The credential is stored in this browser only and is sent solely to the endpoint you configure here.
Production note. A browser-held credential and a direct cross-origin POST suit an internal PM system on your own network. For a bank-hosted OMS, route through the server-side relay instead — it keeps the credential off the browser and out of reach of anyone with access to this machine.
